brief: A small-parts organizer with at least six separate bins.

requirements.evidence: 6 separate bins: bin:-1,0,0 and bin:0,1,0 (open, hex-bin-full), bin:0,-1,0 and bin:1,-1,0 (2 compartments each), bin:0,0,0 and bin:1,0,0 (3 compartments each). That makes 14 sections in total.

The divided bins keep different small parts apart. The demo props (piles of M3 screws, nuts and standoffs) fit in every section. The final check found no prop warnings. The piles sit below the bin rims, so they are hard to see from the side but in plain view from above.
capOpenFaces put solid end caps on the 18 open faces. lockJoints added 9 joint bolts, so the 6 cells can't slide apart. Total: 30 parts.

finish.summary: Small-parts organizer: 6 hex cells side by side on one level, each holding its own full-depth drop-in bin. Two bins are open, two have 2 compartments and two have 3, so there are 14 sections in total. The open faces are capped and the joints bolted together. For the demo I filled the bins with piles of M3 screws, nuts and standoffs. From above you can see every prop. The final check passed with no rule issues and no clashes between parts.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
